sources.fullCitation: ‘Le dernier déjeuner du “Canard aux Navets”.’ Comœdia (Paris), 15 March 1922, p. 2. Group photograph with a row-by-row caption naming Jean Legrand. Bibliothèque nationale de France / RetroNews.
sources.title: Jean-René Legrand in the ‘Canard aux Navets’ group photograph
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.researchNote: The caption identifies the participants by row. Under ‘Tout en haut’, it lists J.-L. Croze, Boissyvon, Jean Legrand, Jean Pascal, René Hervil, Robert Saidreau and René Jeanne, placing Jean Legrand third from the left in the top row. The article text separately names ‘André et Jean Legrand’ and later Lucienne Legrand, so the three people are not being conflated. In this early French-film context, Jean Legrand is Jean-René Legrand, Henri-André Legrand’s brother and collaborator. The media record uses a faithful crop of the captioned figure and does not reconstruct or retouch the face.

media.title: Jean-René Legrand at the ‘Canard aux Navets’ luncheon, 1922
media.description: Portrait detail of the film director Jean-René Legrand from a group photograph published in Comœdia on 15 March 1922. The printed caption identifies the people by row and names ‘Jean Legrand’ as the third person in the top row; the accompanying report separately lists ‘André et Jean Legrand’ among the guests.
media.altText: Small halftone newspaper portrait of the young Jean-René Legrand in formal evening dress and a bow tie, standing in the back row of a group photograph.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph was published in France in 1922 without a photographer or agency credit and is treated as an anonymous work whose seventy-year French term expired at the end of 1992; publication before 1931 also places it in the public domain in the United States.
media.publicCaption: Jean-René Legrand at the ‘Canard aux Navets’ luncheon in Paris, 1922: a detail from the group photograph in Comœdia, where the caption names him as the third person in the top row.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; Comœdia, 15 March 1922, p. 2, detail. RetroNews, Bibliothèque nationale de France.
